opportunities.title: KSeF exception and reconciliation autopilot for accounting offices
opportunities.customer: Polish accounting offices and VAT-registered SMEs that receive or issue enough invoices to be inside mandatory KSeF, especially firms running an ERP, bank feed and accounting package that do not share one clean state.
opportunities.problem_trigger: Every received or issued invoice creates a compulsory digital workflow; schema rejections, offline-mode uploads, duplicates, missing attachments, supplier mistakes and mismatches against the ledger or bank become exception work rather than simple invoice creation.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The accounting office or SME would pay per legal entity per month and by invoice-volume tier from its existing accounting or ERP operations budget. The product fee is proposed, not evidenced; the compulsory invoice flow is evidenced, while willingness to add another tool remains unknown.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: An exception-first SaaS layer that polls KSeF, matches invoices to ERP, bank and ledger records, queues offline or failed submissions, assigns a resolution playbook and preserves an audit trail. Sell direct at a monthly entity fee and white-label to accounting offices or ERP resellers.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Reach many end customers through accounting offices, Polish ERP implementers and tax advisers; lead with a no-write shadow audit that reports exceptions before asking for integration rights.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: A privacy-safe corpus of KSeF error signatures, system combinations, resolution steps and time-to-close can improve triage and make reseller support cheaper with every processed exception.
founder_fit: Uses Polish context, data engineering and AI classification without requiring a personal brand.
Can begin as a read-only, low-capital tool and be tested alongside a full-time job.
A reseller model reduces repeated high-energy direct selling.

claims.statement: The Ministry of Finance says KSeF issuing became mandatory on 1 February 2026 for the largest taxpayers and on 1 April 2026 for most others, while receiving through KSeF became mandatory from 1 February 2026.
The Ministry already provides free KSeF tools and permits access through any tool integrated with the KSeF 2.0 API, so basic issuance and retrieval alone is not a defensible paid product.
A cross-system exception layer may be valuable where free tools and incumbent ERPs do not reconcile operational, bank and ledger states.
The frequency and financial cost of unresolved KSeF exceptions in reachable SMEs is not yet known.

contrary_evidence: Free Ministry tools cover issuance and receipt, and established accounting and ERP vendors can add the same exception features.
Businesses with no more than 10,000 PLN gross of monthly invoiced sales retain a temporary issuing exemption through 2026, shrinking the smallest immediate segment.
KSeF is a compulsory workflow, but that fact alone does not prove a separate software budget.
unknowns: Which exception classes remain painful after ERP vendors finish their 2026 integrations?
Can accounting offices grant read-only API access without unacceptable security and professional-liability concerns?
What per-entity price is lower than the verified labor saved and reseller support burden?
opportunities.validation_test: Recruit 10 accounting offices covering at least 200 entities, ingest only permitted exports or read-only API data for 30 days, classify every exception and measure median staff minutes and unresolved value. Ask offices to pay for a second month only where the shadow audit demonstrates at least three times the proposed fee in saved labor or prevented correction work.

opportunities.title: Mobile BDO and waste-pickup workflow for installation contractors
opportunities.customer: Polish photovoltaic, heat-pump, electrical and renovation contractors that generate non-exempt waste away from the office, plus licensed collectors that want lower-friction contractor accounts.
opportunities.problem_trigger: A job creates cable, packaging, insulation, demolition or equipment waste; before handoff the contractor must select the right waste code, create the electronic record or transfer card, estimate mass and coordinate a paid pickup whose price can change with contamination or weight.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The contractor already pays at each container or waste pickup and would pay a small monthly workflow fee or booking take-rate; collectors could fund a white-label version to acquire compliant repeat customers. A 2026 Wielkopolska provider price list evidences paid pickups, but not national willingness to pay for software.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: A mobile job-to-waste record system with photo capture, human-confirmed code suggestions, BDO-ready fields, collector quote and slot comparison, weight reconciliation and a complete project evidence pack. Monetize by contractor subscription plus a disclosed collector booking fee.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Start with the founder's family renewable installer as a design partner, then distribute through waste collectors, electrical and HVAC wholesalers, installer associations and field-service software vendors.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: Local data linking job type, waste code, photos, estimated versus measured weight, contamination surcharge, collector price and service reliability can improve quoting and reduce rejected or repriced pickups.
founder_fit: Direct pilot access through the family renewable-energy company.
Combines mobile workflow automation, data quality and a marketplace without large initial capital.
Can expand from one contractor niche to other field-service trades.

claims.statement: The Ministry says covered entities conduct waste records and reporting electronically in BDO, while specified low-volume waste categories are exempt.

PGK Śrem's price list effective 16 March 2026 lists gross prices from 498 PLN to 3,591 PLN for mixed renovation and construction-waste container pickups, showing a concrete paid event in part of Wielkopolska; it is one provider and is not a national price benchmark.
Embedding compliant paperwork into the pickup transaction could be more monetizable than selling BDO form entry by itself.
The rate of rejected cards, miscoded waste and avoidable surcharges among small installation contractors is unknown.

contrary_evidence: BDO itself is a government system and small quantities of listed wastes are exempt.
Collectors or office staff may already prepare cards as part of the pickup relationship.
Automated code suggestions create environmental and financial liability if presented without human confirmation.
unknowns: Which installer waste streams are consistently inside BDO rather than municipal or quantity exemptions?
Do collectors permit booking and status integrations, or would the first version require manual coordination?
Is the price spread or paperwork burden large enough to support a take-rate after customer support?
opportunities.validation_test: Instrument 30 real waste handoffs from the family installer and four unrelated contractors, recording staff time, corrections, measured-weight variance, surcharges and quote spread. Obtain two collector partners and charge for a ten-job white-label pilot only after proving faster compliant handoff or lower total pickup cost.

opportunities.title: Inspection operating system and dispatch network for property managers
opportunities.customer: Polish housing-community managers, small commercial-property portfolios, municipal property units and qualified building, electrical and gas inspectors.
opportunities.problem_trigger: A building reaches an annual, five-year or large-building twice-yearly inspection deadline, or an external event triggers an additional safety inspection; asset lists, contractor availability, protocols, defect follow-up and c-KOB-ready evidence must line up.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The owner or property manager already tenders or buys each qualified inspection. Charge per building per year for the compliance calendar and take a transparent dispatch margin on inspections; a Warsaw public procurement plan demonstrates a real budget but is not representative of private portfolios.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: A building register that calculates due dates, bundles scopes, dispatches verified inspectors, checks protocol completeness from photos and measurements, tracks defect remediation and exports a c-KOB-ready evidence packet. Start as managed software for private managers before pursuing public tenders.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Partner with licensed electricians and inspectors, property-management software vendors and insurers; use the family installation network to seed electrical inspection supply in Wielkopolska.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: Structured defect frequencies, remediation cost, building type, inspector reliability and repeat-failure data can improve quoting, routing and preventive recommendations.
founder_fit: Connects family-business electrical capability with an automation and data layer.
Can begin locally with a managed marketplace and become software-led.
Does not require the founder to perform regulated inspections personally.

claims.statement: GUNB states that buildings require at least five-year technical checks including electrical and lightning-protection installations, and large buildings can require checks twice yearly.

ZGN Wola's 2026 procurement plan budgeted 200,000 PLN gross for five-year building, sanitary and electrical inspections, evidencing a specific existing inspection budget rather than the size of the national market.
A combined calendar, protocol-QA and contractor-dispatch product may capture more value than a generic reminder tool.
The willingness of private managers to pay a separate software fee above the inspection contract is unknown.

contrary_evidence: c-KOB and established property-management systems already store part of the statutory record.
Inspection purchasing is price-sensitive, regulated work must remain with qualified people and public procurement has long sales cycles.
Five-year work alone is not recurring enough; the product must aggregate annual, event-triggered and remediation workflows.
unknowns: Whether c-KOB supports a practical integration or only manual export and entry.
Inspector supply density and gross margin after travel, insurance and rework.
Which private segment has enough buildings to value scheduling but is not locked into a national facilities provider?
opportunities.validation_test: Import the calendars of five managers covering at least 200 buildings, identify due or incomplete inspections, and run one inspection cycle with two licensed partners. Seek a paid per-building renewal only if protocol QA and routing cut manager administration by at least half without increasing the inspection price.

opportunities.title: F-gas service-compliance scheduler for multi-site equipment fleets
opportunities.customer: Polish and CEE supermarkets, hotels, clinics, warehouses and other multi-site operators of covered refrigeration, air-conditioning or heat-pump equipment, sold through HVAC service companies.
opportunities.problem_trigger: A covered asset reaches its three-, six- or twelve-month leak-check window, changes refrigerant charge, is repaired after leakage or lacks a complete record; the check must be performed by a certified person.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The equipment operator pays for certified service visits where it lacks qualified in-house staff. The service contractor would pay per managed asset or bundle the software into a maintenance contract; the regulation proves the workflow, not the level of outsourced-service spend.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: OCR equipment nameplates and service documents into an asset register, calculate thresholds and deadlines, alert on sensor or consumption anomalies, dispatch certified technicians and produce regulator-ready records. Sell white-label per asset per month to regional HVAC contractors.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: HVAC installers, refrigeration wholesalers, refrigerant suppliers and insurers already touch the equipment owner; the family renewable network can provide a local heat-pump-adjacent pilot channel.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: An equipment and refrigerant graph linked to leak incidence, service action, technician, parts and time-to-repair can improve preventive scheduling and contractor pricing.
founder_fit: Strong renewable-installation adjacency and an accessible local service-business pilot.
Uses OCR, anomaly detection and operations automation rather than hardware manufacturing.
A white-label contractor channel limits constant end-customer selling.

claims.statement: EU Regulation 2024/573 requires covered equipment leak checks by certified persons at frequencies that can be every 12, six or three months depending on refrigerant quantity, with longer intervals where qualifying detection systems are installed.
A service-company system that converts equipment records into due work orders could turn a mandatory interval into repeat revenue for the contractor.
The number of reachable Polish or CEE multi-site assets above the thresholds and not already managed by enterprise HVAC software is unknown.

contrary_evidence: HVAC service contractors often include logs and reminders in existing maintenance contracts.
Equipment using lower-impact or natural refrigerants may sit outside the same recurring F-gas check burden.
National registers and local implementation details can overlap with or constrain the workflow.
unknowns: Asset counts and service revenue per applicable refrigerant and charge band.
Whether technicians will reliably capture structured data on site.
Cross-border differences in certification, record submission and data retention.
opportunities.validation_test: Partner with two regional HVAC service firms, digitize 200 asset records and compare calculated deadlines with their current schedules. Run a paid three-month white-label pilot only for assets where the tool finds missing, late or duplicate service work and measure recovered visits, technician time and customer churn.

opportunities.title: UDT preflight and commissioning evidence for public EV chargers
opportunities.customer: Polish charge-point operators, property owners and EV-charger installers preparing public stations or returning stations to service after repair or modernization.
opportunities.problem_trigger: Before operation, or after a repair or modernization that triggers an operational examination, the owner must assemble technical documentation, pass an on-site UDT examination and avoid a negative decision that delays charging revenue.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The operator pays the statutory UDT examination fee after the examination and would pay a fixed preflight fee per site for a submission-ready pack. The UDT fee is evidenced; the private preflight budget and value of avoided delay require validation.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: A model-specific document linter, remote commissioning checklist, annotated evidence vault and licensed-electrician review that produces a UDT submission pack and tracks requested corrections. Charge per connector or site without promising approval or preferential scheduling.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Sell through charger distributors, installers, OCPP back-end providers and commercial-property electricians; the family renewables channel can identify local installers and host sites.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: A labelled database of requested corrections, negative findings, charger models, site configurations and remedial actions can make preflight checks increasingly specific.
founder_fit: Directly adjacent to renewable installation and electrical workflows.
Document intelligence and checklist automation are cheap to prototype.
Per-site work can be channel-led and later expanded into fleet compliance software.

claims.statement: UDT states that public-road-transport charging stations and charging points are subject to its technical examinations for safe operation, repair and modernization.
UDT states that examination fees are tied to the prior-year average wage and paid after the examination or opinion, creating a concrete statutory paid event.
A model-specific preflight product may reduce correction cycles and revenue delay, but UDT does not publish enough rejection data here to establish the size of that saving.
Current first-pass failure rates and average days lost to documentation corrections are unknown.

contrary_evidence: UDT publishes forms and guidance, while charger manufacturers and competent installers may already deliver complete packs.
The statutory examination fee belongs to UDT and is not addressable revenue; only incremental preparation value is capturable.
Low inspection failure rates would collapse the value proposition.
unknowns: How many new, repaired or modernized public sites per year are accessible through small and mid-sized installers?
Which documentation defects are machine-checkable versus dependent on an on-site licensed judgment?
Professional-liability and insurance requirements for a paid preflight opinion.
opportunities.validation_test: Obtain 50 anonymized historical submission packs and outcomes from at least 10 installers, build a blind defect checklist and measure whether it predicts every correction without false assurances. Offer five paid preflights with a refund of the service fee if a document defect within the declared scope is missed.

opportunities.title: Reactive-power and contracted-capacity leakage auditor
opportunities.customer: Polish SMEs and multi-site operators on non-household electricity tariffs, particularly facilities with motors, refrigeration, LED lighting, UPS systems, photovoltaic installations or recent electrical modifications.
opportunities.problem_trigger: A monthly distribution invoice starts or continues charging for excess reactive power, excess contracted capacity or a poorly matched tariff, often after load or equipment changes that finance staff cannot interpret.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The facility pays the distribution bill every month. Charge a contingency share of independently verified savings for the first year, plus an optional monitoring subscription; hardware and electrician work remain separately quoted.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: Invoice and interval-data ingestion that identifies charge components, simulates tariff and capacity choices, flags reactive-power patterns, routes a scoped measurement visit and verifies savings after compensation equipment or contract changes.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Acquire customers through accountants, energy brokers, electricians, photovoltaic installers and the founder's family business; begin with a no-saving, no-fee invoice audit.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: A cross-DSO dataset of invoice formats, facility load signatures, interventions, equipment cost and realized savings can improve eligibility scoring and avoid uneconomic site visits.
founder_fit: Excellent match for quantitative modeling and family access to electrical customers.
Success-fee validation controls customer and founder downside.
Can start as analysis software with partner-delivered hardware installation.

claims.statement: URE explains that distribution tariffs contain charges for excess reactive power and contracted-capacity exceedance, and that reactive-power compensation, contract-power changes or tariff changes can reduce specific bill items.
URE specifically recommends analyzing distribution invoices and consumption profiles before cost-saving action.
A verified-savings contract may be easier to buy than a generic energy audit because payment follows a measurable reduction.
The distribution of recoverable annual savings among reachable Polish SMEs under current 2026 tariffs is unknown.

contrary_evidence: Electricians, energy brokers and compensation-equipment vendors already offer audits, sometimes free to sell hardware.
The cited URE explanation establishes charge mechanics but not current tariff amounts or the size of the addressable leakage.
Some sites need capital equipment with long payback, and savings can be confounded by production changes.
unknowns: Share of audited SMEs with enough avoidable charges to support acquisition and electrician costs.
Availability and permissioning of interval meter data across DSOs.
A measurement and verification method robust to weather, occupancy and production changes.
opportunities.validation_test: Audit 100 recent invoices from at least 30 unrelated firms reached through accountants and installers, then meter the 10 strongest sites before any intervention. Request signed contingency agreements only where a conservative payback is under 12 months and verify savings against a pre-agreed baseline for three billing cycles.

opportunities.title: OZE curtailment compensation and deadline recovery service
opportunities.customer: Polish commercial and utility-scale photovoltaic or wind owners, asset managers and O&M firms whose installations actually receive non-market redispatch instructions; residential prosumers are not the target.
opportunities.problem_trigger: PSE or the relevant operator orders generation reduction, creating lost production, telemetry and support-scheme calculations, a 14-day information deadline in some cases and a compensation workflow that can be under-documented or missed.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The asset owner pays a success fee only after incremental compensation is recovered, or a per-MW monitoring fee for event detection and deadline handling. Avoided loss is not automatically capturable revenue; only documented, incremental recovery is billable.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: Detect curtailment events, reconstruct a transparent counterfactual production baseline, reconcile operator and plant data, create the evidence and deadline pack, and hand legal disputes to a specialist partner. Price primarily as a percentage of incremental cash actually collected.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Partner with photovoltaic O&M firms, lenders, insurers, asset-management software and larger installers; use the family renewables network to locate initial commercial assets but not assume they are eligible.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: Plant-level weather, telemetry, dispatch, support-scheme and settlement outcomes can improve counterfactual estimates and reveal which claim paths actually recover money.
founder_fit: Strong data-science problem with direct renewable-energy family adjacency.
Contingency pricing permits low-risk pilots without large capital.
The founder can own analytics while regulated dispute work is partnered.

claims.statement: PSE states that renewable installations that execute non-market redispatch instructions have a right to financial compensation for energy that would otherwise have been produced.

PSE states that, for relevant post-7 September 2023 events, a producer has 14 days from the instruction to provide specified support-scheme information, and failure can exclude that component from the compensation calculation.
A success-fee recovery service is viable only if owners leave material valid compensation unclaimed or under-calculated; the existence of curtailment alone does not prove that leakage.
The frequency, average claim size and current under-recovery rate for reachable independent assets are unknown.

contrary_evidence: PSE provides a defined portal and process, and professional asset managers may already claim correctly.
Only installations that actually receive and execute qualifying instructions are relevant; broad photovoltaic counts overstate the market.
Counterfactual generation and support-scheme treatment can create technical and legal disputes that software cannot settle alone.
unknowns: Number of independently owned eligible plants and concentration among large professional operators.
Access to interval telemetry, dispatch messages and past settlement records.
Whether compensation calculation errors are frequent enough to exceed expert and customer-acquisition cost.
opportunities.validation_test: With owner permission, backtest at least 20 curtailed assets across multiple events, reproduce the official calculation and compare entitlement, submission timing and cash received. Offer contingency contracts only on documented gaps and require three successful incremental recoveries before building a subscription product.

opportunities.title: KSeF-connected late-payment early warning and recovery workflow
opportunities.customer: Polish B2B SMEs issuing roughly 50 to 500 invoices per month, especially exporters and construction, logistics or health suppliers whose owners or finance teams manually chase receivables.
opportunities.problem_trigger: A due date approaches or passes, an expected payment is missing and staff must decide whom to contact, what evidence to attach, when to escalate and whether to use legal collection or factoring without harming the customer relationship.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The supplier would pay per entity per month plus a percentage of overdue cash collected after the workflow starts; factoring or legal handoff can pay a referral fee where disclosed. Recurring late-payment pain is evidenced, but recurring willingness to buy this specific layer is not.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: Connect KSeF or accounting exports and bank transactions, score expected payment timing, automate respectful evidence-backed reminders, track promises to pay and route only unresolved cases to a human, collection partner or factor. Separate prediction from any regulated credit decision.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Embed through accounting offices, KSeF integrators, SME banks, factoring brokers and trade-credit insurers rather than relying on founder-led outbound sales.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: With lawful permissions, an anonymized record of payer timing, invoice features, reminder sequence and recovery outcome can improve prioritization and reveal which intervention works for each segment.
founder_fit: Strong finance, data-science and automation alignment.
KSeF creates a Poland-specific data-access wedge that can later generalize to EU e-invoicing.
Outcome pricing and accounting-channel distribution support part-time validation.

claims.statement: The EU Payment Observatory's 2025 annual report says more than half of EU companies reported difficulties from late payments in 2024 and suppliers reported average B2B and government-to-business payment periods above 60 days.
The same report identifies pursuing late payments as a significant administrative burden, supporting workflow pain but not a software purchase budget.
Invoice and bank data could predict and prioritize collection work, but the incremental recovery over ordinary reminders must be demonstrated experimentally.
Reachable Polish invoice volume, debtor-data legality and willingness to pay a success fee are unknown.

contrary_evidence: Accounting systems, collection agencies, factors and trade-credit insurers already address parts of the workflow.
Payment delay can reflect a genuine dispute or insolvency that better reminders cannot solve.
A cross-customer debtor graph raises confidentiality, GDPR, accuracy and possible credit-scoring concerns.
unknowns: Incremental cash recovery and days-sales-outstanding improvement versus a disciplined manual baseline.
Whether KSeF and bank permissions are acceptable to accounting offices and their clients.
Customer concentration, dispute incidence and legal-collection conversion economics.
opportunities.validation_test: Run a permissioned shadow study over at least 5,000 invoices from 10 SMEs, then randomize eligible overdue invoices between the existing process and a human-approved automated sequence. Charge only a share of incremental cash collected inside a fixed window and stop if relationship complaints or disputed-invoice escalation rises.

opportunities.title: Cross-processor chargeback evidence autopilot for CEE merchants
opportunities.customer: Polish and CEE e-commerce, subscription, travel and digital-service merchants with recurring card disputes across more than one processor or sales channel.
opportunities.problem_trigger: A dispute immediately removes the transaction amount and adds fees; the merchant must collect order, delivery, login, refund-policy and customer-communication evidence before a network deadline, then learn why similar cases recur.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The merchant pays at each dispute through lost funds and processor fees. Charge a percentage of the disputed amount only when won, or a fixed reviewed-submission fee for high-volume teams.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: A cross-processor evidence collector that maps reason codes to the strongest available order, fulfillment, device and communication proof, requires merchant approval, submits a concise pack and reports root causes upstream to checkout and support teams.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Distribute through e-commerce agencies, Shopify and WooCommerce implementers, fulfillment providers, accountants and processor app ecosystems; focus on cross-processor or CEE-language workflows an incumbent processor cannot see.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: Outcome-labelled evidence by reason code, network, issuer region, vertical and evidence type can improve pack selection and identify operational changes that prevent repeat disputes.
founder_fit: A bounded data-integration and document-intelligence product with global expansion potential.
Success pricing permits cheap merchant validation.
Agency distribution and automated onboarding avoid personal-brand selling.

claims.statement: Stripe's Poland pricing page lists a 90 PLN dispute-received fee and a 90 PLN manually countered fee that is returned for won disputes but retained for lost ones; it also prices its own Smart Disputes at 30% of the disputed amount won.
Stripe says relevant evidence can overturn an invalid chargeback and a fully favorable resolution returns the disputed amount, establishing a measurable outcome event.
A cross-processor, vertical-specific product may find a niche despite processor-native automation, but it needs a demonstrable win-rate or labor advantage.
Dispute volume and achievable incremental win rate among reachable CEE merchants are unknown.

contrary_evidence: Stripe already sells AI-prepared Smart Disputes on outcome pricing, providing direct product validation and formidable competition.
Processor and card-network rules limit what evidence matters, and merchants with poor fulfillment cannot automate their way to valid wins.
Low-volume merchants will not support integration cost, while high-volume merchants may have internal risk teams.
unknowns: Which merchant vertical and processor mix has enough disputes but weak native tooling?
API access, submission rights and evidence retention rules across processors.
Whether better evidence or upstream prevention creates the larger and more defensible value.
opportunities.validation_test: Backtest 100 closed disputes from at least five merchants without seeing outcomes, then prospectively prepare 50 human-approved packs and compare completeness, labor minutes and win rate with each merchant's normal process. Accept contingency revenue only on cases where the product supplied material evidence absent from the baseline.

opportunities.title: CBAM supplier-data and certificate-liability cockpit
opportunities.customer: Polish and CEE importers and indirect customs representatives handling more than 50 tonnes per year of covered cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilizer, electricity or hydrogen goods.
opportunities.problem_trigger: Each in-scope import creates embedded-emissions data requirements and a future certificate liability; the importer must maintain authorized status, collect installation data or defaults, prove foreign carbon price where relevant, forecast certificate cash and complete the annual declaration and surrender.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The importer bears the mandatory certificate liability tied to emissions and would pay an annual platform fee plus supplier or customs-line volume pricing. Certificate purchase is concrete; a separate compliance-software budget is not established by regulation and must be validated.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: Ingest customs lines, map CN codes, open a multilingual supplier evidence portal, validate units and periods, flag when defaults or verification are required, forecast certificate quantity and price exposure and preserve deductions for carbon price paid abroad.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Partner with customs brokers, freight forwarders, metal and fertilizer distributors, accountants and trade-finance banks; sell a fixed-fee liability diagnostic before an annual contract.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: Reusable supplier-installation records, CN mappings, evidence-quality scores, verified emission histories and resolution patterns can reduce repeated requests across importer customers while respecting confidentiality.
founder_fit: Strong EU, finance, quantitative and data-workflow fit.
Can start with software and managed data validation rather than capital-intensive operations.
Broker distribution can reach importers without a public founder persona.

claims.statement: The European Commission says the definitive CBAM regime applies from 1 January 2026 and importers above the 50-tonne threshold must become authorized declarants, declare embedded emissions and surrender purchased certificates.

The Commission published 2026 quarterly certificate prices of 75.36 EUR for Q1 and 75.28 EUR for Q2 and says purchases on the common platform begin from February 2027, making 2026 imports a measurable upcoming cash liability rather than an August 2026 certificate purchase.

The 50-tonne simplification is expected by the Commission to exempt about 182,000 importers while retaining over 99% of covered emissions, concentrating the opportunity in fewer, generally larger accounts.
Supplier-data reuse and liability forecasting may support SaaS margins, but regulation does not prove customers will buy from a new vendor.

contrary_evidence: The 50-tonne threshold removes most small importers, leaving accounts with longer security, procurement and liability reviews.
Customs brokers, ERP vendors and major consultancies are natural incumbents, and default emission values may reduce near-term supplier-data urgency.
Regulatory changes, circumvention rules and certificate timing can change product requirements.
unknowns: Number and import concentration of reachable above-threshold Polish and CEE firms by sector.
How much compliance work customs representatives already bundle and at what price.
Supplier willingness to share installation data and the legal ability to reuse it across importers.
opportunities.validation_test: Obtain permissioned 2026 customs extracts from 25 potential importers, calculate scope and certificate liability using both actual and allowed default data, and quantify missing evidence and forecast variance. Sell the diagnostic at a fixed fee, then require at least three annual contracts through one broker before building deeper registry integrations.

opportunities.title: e-TOLL reconciliation and route-cost control for Polish fleets
opportunities.customer: Polish road hauliers, bus operators and field-service fleets with roughly 10 to 200 heavy vehicles that already use an OBU or external location system but reconcile tolls manually.
opportunities.problem_trigger: Every trip over the paid network generates a per-kilometre charge based on vehicle category and emission class; device outages, vehicle-master errors, route deviations, low prepaid balance or rate changes create exceptions, administrative risk or avoidable cost.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The fleet pays tolls as trips occur and reconciles them monthly. Charge per vehicle per month for anomaly and route-cost control, with a separate success fee only for verified refunds or avoided misclassification.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: Reconcile dispatch and telematics tracks against e-TOLL notes, verify vehicle and emission-class masters, alert on data gaps or unusual charges, simulate route toll cost alongside time and fuel, and assemble a traceable claim pack for human submission.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Embed with OBU and ZSL providers, fuel-card issuers, transport accountants and telematics integrators; sell first as an audit report through partners rather than another driver app.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: A route-section, vehicle, rate, device-state and confirmed-anomaly dataset can make reconciliation faster and reveal recurring issues by hardware or fleet workflow.
founder_fit: Quantitative reconciliation and anomaly detection match the founder's data-science skills.
Poland supplies a focused regulatory wedge with a large recorded vehicle base.
Telematics partners can provide scalable distribution without camera-based marketing.

claims.statement: KAS reports over 3.2 million registered heavy vehicles, about 5,870 kilometres of paid roads and a legal obligation for vehicles over 3.5 tonnes and buses using covered roads to pay through e-TOLL.
KAS changed heavy-vehicle rates from 1 January 2026, and its classifier states that the rate depends on vehicle mass category, emission class and road class.
Reconciling tolls to dispatch and telematics may expose errors or route savings, but total registered vehicles are not the same as an affordably reachable paying market.
The incidence and recoverable value of overcharges or preventable exceptions in 10-to-200-vehicle fleets is unknown.

contrary_evidence: KAS provides a free driver app and account portal, while EETS and telematics providers already combine toll services for many fleets.
A cheaper toll route can cost more in fuel, driver time or delivery performance, so optimization must model total trip economics.
The reported 3.2 million registered vehicles describe system scale, not unique active customers or accessible SMEs.
unknowns: Billing-data export or API availability and partner permissioning.
Frequency of vehicle-master, route and device anomalies that lead to money recovery rather than only alerts.
Partner revenue share and support cost per vehicle.
opportunities.validation_test: Run a three-month read-only reconciliation over at least 20 fleets and one million vehicle-kilometres, classify every mismatch and verify each with the fleet before assigning value. Pre-sell through one OBU or accounting partner only if verified annual recovery plus admin savings exceeds three times the proposed annual subscription.

opportunities.title: Occupational-medicine booking and eligibility orchestration for SMEs
opportunities.customer: Polish employers with 20 to 500 workers, staffing agencies and multi-site service or industrial firms that repeatedly arrange pre-employment, periodic and return-to-work medical examinations.
opportunities.problem_trigger: A hire, job change, certificate expiry or return after qualifying absence requires the employer to create a correct hazard-specific referral, find an appointment, preserve the certificate and avoid scheduling a worker who is not medically cleared.
opportunities.payer_and_paid_event: The employer is legally responsible for the full examination cost and associated paid work time and travel. Charge per completed examination or per active employee per month, sharing booking revenue with participating occupational-medicine clinics.
opportunities.offer_and_business_model: A non-diagnostic rules and booking layer that creates referral drafts from role and hazard templates, checks completeness, alerts on expiry, offers clinic slots, tracks attendance and stores access-controlled proof of eligibility without retaining unnecessary clinical findings.
opportunities.distribution_mechanism: Distribute through payroll bureaus, staffing agencies, HR software, insurers and regional clinic groups; use medical-domain understanding for workflow design but leave every medical judgment to licensed clinicians.
opportunities.compounding_advantage: Privacy-minimized data on appointment lead time, no-shows, referral defects, job-hazard pathways and clinic reliability can improve routing and employer capacity planning without building a diagnosis database.
founder_fit: Combines health interest, a nearby medical perspective and automation skills.
Per-exam transactions allow a low-capital marketplace test before software build-out.
Payroll and clinic distribution reduce the need for constant direct selling.

claims.statement: The Polish Labour Inspectorate states that employers fully bear the costs of pre-employment, periodic and control examinations, including the examination, paid work time, specified repeat examinations and travel.

The Ministry states that an employer cannot admit a worker without a current medical certificate for the specified role and conditions and must issue the referral with hazard and working-condition information.
Faster booking and cleaner referrals may reduce paid downtime and failed visits, but the employer's mandatory spend does not automatically create willingness to pay an intermediary.
Current appointment lead times, no-show rates, referral-error rates and clinic margin available to an intermediary are unknown.

contrary_evidence: Large occupational-medicine providers already sell employer subscriptions and online booking.
Many SMEs have direct local clinic relationships and may see no need for another system.
Medical and employment data create high privacy, security and role-boundary requirements.
unknowns: Which employer segment suffers enough lead-time or referral friction to switch or add a booking layer?
Clinic API readiness, appointment inventory and per-exam contribution margin.
The minimum data architecture that supports eligibility while avoiding unnecessary health information.
opportunities.validation_test: Coordinate 200 examinations for one staffing agency and three independent clinics using a manual concierge plus a simple employer portal; compare appointment lead time, no-shows, referral corrections and employer admin minutes with the prior process. Charge per completed appointment and proceed only if employers reorder and clinics retain positive contribution margin.
